record.detail: The hypotheses are: X is connected, compact, Kähler; theta is a smooth closed real (1,1)-form; PSH(X,theta) is nonempty. The quotient ranges only over equivalence classes induced by actual theta-psh potentials, where equivalence means equality of all integral multiplier-ideal levels, equivalently the divisorial Lelong profile in the source-dependent valuative package. No arbitrary formal ideal tower or valuative datum is asserted realizable. The target is the canonical normalized I-model representative and a counterexample to descent of raw mass, not reconstruction of an arbitrary representative.
record.location: Statement, setup and definition of realizable \(\mathcal I\)-data

record.detail: The competitor family consists of theta-psh functions bounded above by zero in the fixed realizable I-class d. It is nonempty: a compact quasi-psh function has finite supremum, subtracting that finite constant preserves theta-psh status and all multiplier ideals and makes the supremum zero, hence the function is at most zero.

A finite maximum of theta-psh functions is theta-psh and remains at most zero. For every prime divisor over X, the generic divisorial Lelong number of max(psi_1,psi_2) is the minimum of the two generic Lelong numbers. Since both inputs have the same divisorial profile d, the maximum has that profile too; the valuative multiplier-ideal criterion at every positive integral scaling then gives the same full ideal tower. Induction gives closure under arbitrary finite maxima.
record.location: Proof, first paragraph: closure of \(\mathcal F_d\) under finite maxima

record.detail: Choquet's lemma supplies a countable sequence whose regularized supremum is U. Finite maxima u_j stay in the competitor family and increase almost everywhere to U. For a fixed prime divisor E on a model, a point can be chosen outside the countable union of exceptional analytic subsets for all pullbacks u_j and U, so point and generic Lelong numbers agree simultaneously. After addition of a smooth local potential, the local functions are psh and the increasing-limit theorem applies, with Lelong numbers decreasing to that of the a.e. limit. Every u_j has profile d, hence nu(U,E)=nu(d,E). This is repeated for each E; no single point common to different divisors is required.
record.location: Proof, second paragraph: Choquet sequence and preservation of divisorial Lelong numbers

record.detail: Equality of all divisorial Lelong numbers for U and a representative of d, followed by the valuative criterion for each positive integral multiple, yields equality of every multiplier ideal in the tower. Thus U lies in F_d. Since U is the upper envelope and itself a competitor, it is the largest member. The definition of F_d uses only d, not the chosen representative phi, so the envelope and R_theta(d) are independent of representatives. The quotient is restricted to realizable d, which supplies the initial competitor.
record.location: Proof, second paragraph: \([U]_{\mathcal I}=d\), largest competitor, and representative-independence

record.detail: Because U is the largest competitor and belongs to its own class, applying the same envelope to U returns U, giving the I-model fixed-point property. If sup_X U were negative, a sufficiently small positive constant could be added while retaining the bound by zero, theta-psh status, and multiplier ideals, contradicting maximality; hence sup_X U=0. Any normalized I-model potential in d is a fixed point of the identical competitor envelope and therefore equals U. This proves existence and uniqueness without a nonpluripolar-mass hypothesis.
record.location: Proof, end of first-assertion argument: normalization, idempotence, and uniqueness

record.detail: With ell_0=1 and ell_m=exp(-4^m), the explicit inequalities 2 ell_1<ell_0 and 2 ell_{m+1}<ell_m allow two children at every stage. Assigning mass 2^{-m} to each stage-m interval is consistent and yields a probability measure supported on the limiting compact set. Any point is contained in at most a bounded number of stage-m intervals, so its mass is bounded by a constant times 2^{-m} and is zero; the limiting measure is nonatomic. The capacity criterion has summands 2^{-m} log(1/ell_m)=2^m, so the series diverges. Rescaling the initial circle length changes the logarithms by a bounded additive constant and does not affect divergence. Hence the compact support F has logarithmic capacity zero and is polar/pluripolar on P^1.

For each p on P^1 the normalized Green potential satisfies omega+dd^c G_p=delta_p and sup G_p=0. Integration against the probability measure defines an upper-bounded potential G_mu. At any point outside the compact support F, positive distance from F uniformly bounds the logarithmic kernels below, so G_mu is finite there and is not identically minus infinity. Distributional Fubini gives omega+dd^c G_mu=mu, a positive order-zero current/measure of total mass one supported on F. Thus phi_s=sG_mu is omega-psh and omega+dd^c phi_s=(1-s)omega+s mu for 0<=s<=1.
record.location: Proof, construction and integration of the Green potentials

record.detail: On a Riemann surface, the Lelong number of the positive (1,1)-current omega+dd^c phi_s at a point is its atomic mass (up to the fixed convention already normalized by the Green equation). Both omega and mu are nonatomic, so every point Lelong number is zero. Birational models of a smooth curve introduce no new divisorial valuations beyond points, so every divisorial Lelong number is zero. Scaling by each positive integer preserves zero, and the valuative multiplier-ideal criterion then puts 1 in I(m phi_s), hence I(m phi_s)=O_X for all m. Therefore every phi_s has the same realizable I-data as 0.
record.location: Proof, vanishing Lelong numbers and scaled multiplier ideals

record.detail: The Green potential G_mu is locally bounded on X\F. By plurifine locality, on X\F the degree-one nonpluripolar product equals the ordinary positive current (1-s)omega+s mu; since mu is supported on F, its restriction there is (1-s)omega. The nonpluripolar product puts no mass on the pluripolar set F, and the smooth area measure also assigns F zero mass. Consequently the global product is exactly (1-s)omega and, under the normalization integral omega=1, its total mass is 1-s. This is equality of positive measures, so no invalid passage from signed mass to total variation is involved.
record.location: Proof, BEGZ degree-one nonpluripolar mass computation

record.detail: All phi_s lie in [0]_I, and the first assertion sends this class to its unique normalized I-model representative. The zero potential is normalized and is its own I-envelope, so that representative is 0. At s=1, phi_1 has nonpluripolar mass zero while the canonical representative 0 has mass one; across the same class the formula gives every mass 1-s. Thus neither the raw representative nor raw nonpluripolar mass descends to the quotient.
record.location: Proof, final paragraph: common canonical representative and failure of raw-mass reconstruction

record.detail: The conclusions are confined to realizable multiplier-ideal data on a compact Kähler manifold and to the explicit projective-line family. The proof does not claim realization of arbitrary formal towers, an all-semivaluation reconstruction formula, recovery of raw mass, a compact-Kähler/transcendental version of the separate projective order isomorphism, or use of the P14.7 terminal-left-limit corollary. The Q-line-bundle limitation and the projective real Neron-Severi setting of the separate comparison theorem remain explicit exclusions.
